mentions.name: Isograph
mentions.description: This incremental compiler for Isograph literals no longer bails on the first error, enabling LSP features like hover and go-to-definition on valid parts of files even in the presence of errors, surfacing errors in VSCode, and providing auto-fixes that generate the Isograph literal declaring a selected missing field.
mentions.problem: The previous batch compiler bailed on the first error, preventing LSP results on unbroken code and making errors harder to surface and fix in the editor.
mentions.audience: Developers working with Isograph literals in editors like VSCode, who want better error reporting and tooling despite compile errors.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Just released the next version of Isograph https://isograph.dev/blog/2025/12/14/isograph-0.5.0/

TLDR the incremental compiler rewrite is finally bearing fruit. Namely, because we no longer have a batch compiler (i.e. we don't bail on the first error), we can

- provide LSP results (hover, goto def, etc) on non-broken parts of your isograph literals, even in the presence of errors
